examples.en: This book is co-authored by two professors.
The paper we published together won an award.
I'm preparing a co-authored book with a friend.

examples.ko: 공저자 이름이 표지에 나란히 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The co-authors' names are printed side by side on the cover.

examples.ko: 이 책은 공저라서 장마다 쓴 사람이 달라요.
examples.en: Since this book is co-authored, each chapter has a different writer.
It's my first co-authoring project, so I'm very nervous.

explain: 혼자 쓴 책은 '단독 저서'라고 해요. 여럿이 함께 쓴 사람은 '공저자'라고 부르고, 함께 번역한 것은 '공역'이라고 해요. 책 소개나 논문에서 주로 써요.

phrases.example: 이 논문의 공저자는 모두 세 명이에요.
phrases.en: This paper has three co-authors in total.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공저'에 사람을 뜻하는 '-자'가 붙어, 함께 쓴 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-자' (person) to 공저 refers to someone who wrote it together with others.

phrases.example: 이 공저서에는 열 명의 글이 실려 있어요.
phrases.en: This co-authored book contains writings by ten people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 함께 쓴 책 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the book itself that several people wrote together.

phrases.en: I published a book co-authored with a senior colleague.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이나 논문을 함께 써서 냈다고 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for publishing a book or paper written jointly.

explain_en: A book written by one person is called a '단독 저서'. People who write together are '공저자', and a joint translation is '공역'. It appears mostly in book descriptions and academic papers.

examples.en: We have a mock interview at school tomorrow.
I did worst in English on the mock exam.
We held a practice drill at the fire station.
I held a mock trial with my classmates.
Try practicing stocks with simulated investing.
It's only a simulated situation, so you don't need to be nervous.

explain: 모의는 단독으로는 거의 안 쓰고 '모의 면접', '모의시험', '모의 훈련'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙어요. 수능을 준비하는 학생들은 '모의고사'를 자주 봐요. 실제와 똑같이 해 본다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 고등학생들은 한 달에 한 번 모의고사를 봐요.
phrases.en: High school students take a mock exam once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모의'가 들어간 가장 흔한 말로, 실제 시험을 연습하는 시험이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word with '모의', a practice test for the real exam.

phrases.example: 학교에서 불이 났을 때를 생각하며 모의 훈련을 했어요.
phrases.en: At school we did a drill imagining a fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 일이 생겼다고 생각하고 미리 해 보는 연습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A practice run done as if a real event were happening.

phrases.en: I practiced a mock interview with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜 면접 전에 연습으로 하는 면접이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An interview done as practice before a real one.

explain_en: 모의 is almost never used alone; it attaches before another noun, as in 모의 면접, 모의시험, and 모의 훈련. Students preparing for the college entrance exam often take a 모의고사 (practice test). It carries the feeling of doing something exactly as if it were real.

examples.ko: 이 공장에는 이십 년 경력의 숙련공이 많아요.
examples.en: This factory has many skilled workers with twenty years of experience.
It takes several years to become a skilled worker.

examples.ko: 숙련공 한 명이 신입 세 명 몫을 해요.
examples.en: One skilled worker does the work of three newcomers.
The company posted a notice looking for skilled workers.
A machine can hardly match a skilled worker's hand skills.

examples.ko: 숙련공이 부족해서 주문을 다 받지 못하고 있어요.
examples.en: We're short of skilled workers, so we can't take all the orders.

explain: 공장이나 기술 현장에서 오랜 훈련으로 기술을 익힌 노동자를 말해요. 반대말은 '미숙련공'이고, 뉴스나 구인 공고에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: A skilled technician fixes the machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙련공'과 비슷하지만 기술을 가진 사람을 더 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '숙련공' but covers skilled people more broadly.

phrases.en: The factory is looking for skilled workers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구인 공고에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in job postings.

phrases.example: 오 년 일하고 나서 숙련공이 되었어요.
phrases.en: After working five years, I became a skilled worker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랜 훈련 끝에 기술이 능숙해졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming skilled after long training.

explain_en: Skilled manual or industrial worker in a factory or trade. It refers to a worker at a factory or technical site who has built up skills through long training. The opposite is '미숙련공', and you often see the word in the news and in job postings.

examples.ko: 그녀는 유명한 저널리스트가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: She wants to become a famous journalist.
A journalist is taking photos at the scene.
A journalist has to check the facts accurately.
My uncle worked as a journalist for a long time.
I set up an interview with a journalist.
I read a book by a journalist working abroad.

explain: '기자'가 훨씬 흔해요. '저널리스트'는 신문사 소속이 아니어도 글이나 영상으로 취재하는 사람까지 넓게 가리키고, 조금 전문적이고 멋진 느낌이 있어요. 신문사나 방송국에서 일하는 사람은 보통 '기자'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: My older brother is a reporter who works at a newspaper company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '저널리스트'보다 '기자'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, 기자 is used much more often than 저널리스트.

phrases.en: He works as a freelance journalist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에 소속되지 않고 일하는 사람에게는 '저널리스트'가 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: 저널리스트 fits people who work independently, not for one company.

phrases.en: My dream is to be a journalist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿈이에요'와 함께 장래 희망을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 꿈이에요 to talk about a future career goal.
phrases.en_equiv: my dream is to be a journalist

explain_en: Loanword — journalist, often a reporter who covers stories in the field. '기자' is far more common. '저널리스트' can also cover people who report through writing or video without belonging to a newspaper, and it sounds a bit more professional and stylish. People working at a newspaper or broadcaster are usually called '기자'.

t90.ax: She wants to become a famous journalist.

examples.ko: 정비사가 브레이크 오일이 부족하다며 바로 보충해 주었어요.
examples.en: The mechanic said the brake fluid was low and topped it up right away.
I told the car mechanic that the sound was strange.

examples.ko: 정비사는 차 소리만 듣고도 문제를 알아요.
examples.en: A mechanic can tell the problem just by hearing the car.

examples.ko: 형은 십 년째 정비사로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: My older brother has worked as a mechanic for ten years.
After hearing the mechanic's explanation, the repair cost made sense.
The mechanic in our neighborhood is friendly.

explain: 자동차나 비행기 같은 기계를 점검하고 고치는 사람이에요. '자동차 정비사', '항공 정비사'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 말해요.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 자동차 정비사가 되고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling wants to become a car mechanic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 기계를 고치는지 앞에 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase, specifying the type of machine.

phrases.en: An aircraft mechanic checks airplanes carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기를 점검하고 고치는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who inspects and repairs airplanes.

phrases.en: I left my car with the mechanic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고쳐 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone to repair something.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave it with the mechanic

explain_en: It is a person who inspects and repairs machines such as cars and aircraft. People attach the object in front, as in '자동차 정비사' (car mechanic) and '항공 정비사' (aircraft mechanic).

en: to lead; to conduct; to command

examples.en: That person conducts the orchestra.
The firefighter directed the work of putting out the fire.

examples.ko: 다음 연주회는 새로 온 선생님이 지휘할 거예요.
examples.en: The newly arrived teacher will conduct the next concert.
The team leader personally took charge on site.
The voice of the coach directing the game was loud.
The person who led the operation took responsibility.

explain: 음악에서는 손으로 연주를 이끌 때, 일에서는 여러 사람에게 명령을 내려 움직일 때 써요. 회사에서 사람을 이끄는 건 '이끌다'나 '관리하다'가 더 일상적이고, '지휘하다'는 현장·군대·소방처럼 빠르게 지시하는 상황에 잘 맞아요.

phrases.en: When the conductor raised his hand, the performance began.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악에서 연주를 이끄는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who leads a musical performance.

phrases.en: That firefighter took charge of the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 작업 현장에서 지시를 내리는 역할을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to giving orders at an accident or work site.

phrases.en: The team leader leads the team well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 모임에서는 '이끌다'가 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 이끌다 is more everyday for companies and groups.

explain_en: Direct an orchestra, choir or operation. In music it is used for leading a performance with your hands; in work, for giving orders that move many people. For leading people at a company, 이끌다 or 관리하다 is more everyday. 지휘하다 suits on-site, military, or firefighting situations where instructions come fast.

dis.h: direct or command, e.g. an orchestra
gh: lead people or a team, general
lead a group on a trip

p.n: 이끌다 means leading in general and loses the 'conducting music' sense.

en: to flatter; to adulate; to bootlick

examples.ko: 그 직원은 부장님 옆에서 늘 알랑대요.
examples.en: That employee is always sucking up beside the manager.
It's hard to trust people who fawn.
My friend buttered me up and then asked a favor.
It's no use sucking up to me.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마한테 알랑대며 장난감을 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The child coaxed his mom with sweet talk to buy him a toy.
The fawning way he spoke to customers sounded awkward.

explain: '알랑거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. '-대다'는 같은 행동을 자꾸 하는 느낌이 있어서 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 상대를 낮게 보거나 흉볼 때 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 상사 앞에서 알랑대는 모습이 보기 싫었어요.
phrases.en: I disliked seeing him fawn in front of the boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복해서 비위를 맞추는 행동을 흉볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to disapprove of repeatedly sucking up to someone.

phrases.example: 알랑대지 말고 하고 싶은 말을 해 보세요.
phrases.en: Stop sucking up and say what you want to say.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비위를 맞추는 행동을 그만하라고 말할 때 쓰는 존댓말 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to tell someone to stop sucking up.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 힘 있는 사람에게만 아첨해요.
phrases.en: He only flatters people with power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 입말보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but seen more in writing and news than in speech.

explain_en: Interchangeable with the (-거리다) form (알랑거리다); repeatedly fawning to win favor, disapproving. It means the same as '알랑거리다', so you can swap them. The '-대다' ending gives a feel of repeating the action, which sounds natural in speech. It is often used when looking down on someone or criticizing them.

t90.ax: It's no use sucking up to me.

examples.en: My aunt was a woman soldier for a short time when she was young.

examples.ko: 여군 훈련 영상을 보고 멋있다고 생각했어요.
examples.en: I watched a female soldiers' training video and thought it was cool.
The female soldiers finished the tough training to the end.

examples.ko: 여군으로 지원하려면 체력 검사를 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To apply as a female soldier, you have to pass a fitness test.
A female soldier was the lead in the drama, and it was fun.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 군복은 여군에게도 잘 맞아요.
examples.en: The newly released uniform fits female soldiers well too.

explain: '여자 군인'이라고 풀어 말해도 돼요. 남자 군인은 보통 따로 부르지 않고 그냥 '군인'이라고 해요. 뉴스나 군대 이야기에서 여성 군인을 따로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: My older sister is building her strength to become a woman soldier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여성이 군인이 되는 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a woman becoming a soldier.

phrases.en: A female soldier carried the flag at the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여군'을 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain, spelled-out way of saying '여군'.

phrases.en: That actress is a former woman soldier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 군대에서 복무했던 여성을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a woman who once served in the military.

explain_en: You can also say it as '여자 군인'. Male soldiers are usually just called '군인' without a special word. It is used in news and military talk when speaking about women soldiers specifically.

en: to get discharged; to be transferred

examples.en: My older brother is being discharged next month.
My uncle was discharged last year and got a job at a company.

examples.ko: 전역한 친구와 오랜만에 만나서 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had a meal with my friend who got out of the military, after a long time.

examples.ko: 전역하면 제일 먼저 여행을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: When I'm discharged, I want to go on a trip first.

examples.ko: 전역하는 날 부대 앞에서 가족을 만났어요.
examples.en: On the day of his discharge, he met his family in front of the base.

examples.ko: 그는 이 년 만에 전역해서 대학에 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: He was discharged after two years and returned to university.

explain: 한국에서는 군대 이야기가 흔해서 일상 대화에도 자주 나와요. 군 복무를 끝내고 나가는 걸 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '제대하다'를 더 자주 써요. 군대에 들어가는 건 '입대하다'예요.

phrases.en: My older brother was discharged last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전역하다'와 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 전역하다 and more common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: My older brother's discharge date is next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대를 나가는 날을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the day someone leaves military service.

phrases.en: After being discharged, I went back to university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군 복무를 마친 다음의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what happens after finishing military service.

explain_en: Military service is a common topic in Korea, so this word often comes up in daily talk. It means finishing service and leaving, and 제대하다 is used more often for the same thing. Entering the military is 입대하다.

examples.en: He is, in every sense, the best singer in our country.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 명실공히 문화의 중심지가 되었어요.
examples.en: This city has truly become a center of culture.

examples.ko: 올해부터 명실공히 우리 회사가 업계 일등이에요.
examples.en: From this year, our company is number one in the industry in every sense.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 명실공히 세계 정상에 올랐어요.
examples.en: That player has truly reached the top of the world.

examples.ko: 이 음식은 명실공히 우리 고향의 대표 음식이에요.
examples.en: This dish is truly the signature dish of my hometown.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 명실공히 지역에서 가장 좋은 학교로 인정받아요.
examples.en: This school is rightfully recognized as the best in the region.

explain: 이름만이 아니라 실제로도 그렇다고 인정할 때 써요. '최고', '대표', '중심' 같은 말 앞에서 자주 쓰고, 뉴스나 연설 같은 격식 있는 글에서 많이 보여요. 가벼운 대화에서는 '진짜', '누가 봐도'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: He is truly the best player, in name and in fact.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름과 실제가 서로 맞는다는 뜻으로, 거의 같은 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Meaning name and reality match, it fits almost the same situations.

phrases.example: 이 작품은 명실공히 우리나라를 대표하는 영화예요.
phrases.en: This work is truly a film that represents our country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대표하다'와 함께 쓰면 인정받는 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '대표하다', it points to a position that is rightly recognized.

phrases.en: Anyone can see that team is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '명실공히' 대신 쓰기 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday substitute for '명실공히'.

explain_en: You use it when something is the best or the leading one not only by title but also in fact. It often comes before words like '최고', '대표' and '중심', and shows up in news and speeches. In casual talk people more often say '진짜' or '누가 봐도'.

examples.en: I prefer soft-boiled eggs to hard-boiled ones.
I made a sauce with fully ripe tomatoes.

examples.ko: 그 배우의 연기는 완숙의 경지에 올랐어요.
examples.en: That actor's acting has reached a level of full mastery.

examples.ko: 과일은 완숙이 되기 전에 따면 맛이 없어요.
examples.en: Fruit doesn't taste good if you pick it before it is fully ripe.
To hard-boil it, it takes about ten minutes.
It looks cool to watch him cook with such mature skill.

explain: 달걀은 '완숙'과 '반숙'을 짝으로 말해요. 과일이 푹 익은 것뿐 아니라 솜씨나 연기가 무르익은 것에도 써서 '완숙한 연기'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I boiled the eggs hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달걀을 어느 정도 익힐지 말할 때 '~(으)로' 형태로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~(으)로' to say how done the eggs should be.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 완숙한 연기를 보여 줬어요.
phrases.en: That actor gave a polished, mature performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완숙한 + 명사'로 솜씨가 무르익었다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '완숙한 + noun' praises skill that has fully matured.

phrases.en: Which do you like, hard-boiled or soft-boiled?
phrases.nuance_ko: 달걀을 고를 때 둘을 짝으로 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two are asked together when choosing how to cook an egg.

explain_en: Complete ripeness or mastery; also a fully cooked egg (완숙 달걀) For eggs, '완숙' (hard-boiled) and '반숙' (soft-boiled) are paired. Besides fully ripe fruit, it also describes skill or acting that has matured, as in '완숙한 연기'.

examples.en: The last stop of this bus is in front of Seoul Station.
I finally arrived at the end point of the long trip.

examples.ko: 지하철 종착점까지 가면 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about an hour to go to the end of the subway line.

examples.ko: 우리 토론은 종착점 없이 계속 이어졌어요.
examples.en: Our discussion went on and on with no endpoint.

examples.ko: 마라톤의 종착점이 보이자 다시 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: When I saw the marathon finish, I got my energy back.

examples.ko: 인생의 종착점을 생각하면 지금이 소중하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: When I think about the end of life, the present feels precious.

explain: 버스나 기차가 마지막으로 서는 곳뿐 아니라 여행, 토론, 노력의 끝을 말할 때도 써요. 버스나 지하철에서는 '종점'이라고도 해요. 반대는 '출발점'이에요.

phrases.en: This bus goes all the way to the last stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스나 지하철에서 더 자주 쓰는 짧은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter word used more often for buses and subways.

phrases.example: 이 이야기도 이제 종착점에 가까워지고 있어요.
phrases.en: This story is now nearing its end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 이야기가 끝나 갈 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when something is nearing its end.

phrases.en: This is the starting point and that is the end point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 짝으로 같이 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs the word with its opposite.

explain_en: The last stop point of a bus or train line. It refers to the last stop of a bus or train, and also to the end of a trip, discussion or effort. For buses and subways, people also say '종점'. The opposite is '출발점' (starting point).

en: the highest level; the highest grade

examples.en: The service at this hotel is top grade.
I cooked using only top-quality ingredients.
In grammar class, I learned the English superlative.
That shop sells its fruit at the top grade.

examples.ko: 시험에서 최상급 반에 들어가는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: My goal is to get into the top-level class through the test.
That player's skill belongs to the top level.

explain: '최고'는 가장 높은 하나를 말하고, 최상급은 가장 높은 쪽의 등급을 말해요. 물건, 서비스, 실력, 학급 수준에 써요. 문법에서는 영어의 'the best' 같은 형태도 최상급이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: This fruit is top-quality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 등급이 가장 높다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a product is of the highest grade.

phrases.en: That restaurant is famous for top-level service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서비스나 실력처럼 사람이 하는 일의 수준을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the level of human-provided things like service or skill.

phrases.en: I learned superlative expressions in English class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문법에서 'the best' 같은 형태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In grammar, refers to forms like 'the best'.

explain_en: Highest quality or grade of goods (최상급 과일) 최고 points to the single highest one, while 최상급 points to the top tier of a ranking. It is used for goods, service, skill, and class levels. In grammar, forms like English 'the best' are also called 최상급.
